title: Argentina Warns It Will 'Fully Exercise All Available Actions' Against Falklands Sea Lion Oil Field Development
detail: Argentina's Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a formal diplomatic warning that it would 'fully exercise all available actions' to prevent the development of the Sea Lion oil field in the North Falkland Basin, describing Rockhopper Exploration (UK) and its Israeli partner Navitas Petroleum as 'clandestine' operators. The Sea Lion field — located approximately 220 km north of the Falkland Islands — is estimated to hold 283 million barrels of recoverable oil, with initial production potential of up to 55,000 bbl/day (Phase 1) rising to 125,000 bbl/day (Phase 2). Drilling is planned to commence in 2027. Argentina's warning invokes Law 26,659 (which criminalizes hydrocarbon exploration in Argentine-claimed continental shelf zones without national authorization) and relevant UN resolutions on the Malvinas-Falklands sovereignty dispute. Foreign Minister Diana Mondino characterized the development as 'unlawful.' The Milei government simultaneously announced the purchase of 24 F-16 fighter jets from Denmark — framed as general defense modernization rather than Malvinas-specific — while insisting Argentina's Malvinas posture remains strictly diplomatic. Rockhopper and Navitas dismissed the Argentine warning as legally non-binding given the UK's administrative control of the islands.

media.caption: Argentina warns it will act against Falklands Sea Lion oil field development — June 5, 2026
